knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A cleaner cannot certify compliance across several jurisdictions. The request is refused, the reason is given, and it is referred to the responsible food-safety authority.
Open items are labelled clearly with the decision holder named, so the owner can act on them. Leaving them out or marking them complete misstates the package.
The handover stops where the food-safety owner has not signed or where a trigger applies. Time pressure and a finished clean are not reasons to proceed.

practicalCriteria: Prepares a fictional closeout package listing cleaned zones, exceptions, sign-offs, evidence index and labelled open items, with the decision holder for each open item.
Refuses a simulated universal certificate request without asserting any other country's law as Australian law, and records the referral.
Stops a simulated handover that lacks the food-safety owner's signature, and records the trigger and the pending decision.
Corrects a simulated error using the site method and does not backfill or replace any entry.
passRule: All four practical criteria observed as met in an inert tabletop simulation, with the knowledge check result at least 2 of 3 correct. Knowledge check results and the simulation are not a certification, an audit approval or a release.
evidenceRequired: Fictional closeout package with labelled open items
Refusal and referral record for the certificate request
Stop and refer record for the unsigned handover
Assessor observation note for each practical criterion
stopWorkCriteria: Universal or cross-jurisdiction certificate issued or signed by the learner
Handover completed without the food-safety owner's signature
Record backfilled, replaced or altered without the site correction method
Open items omitted from the closeout package
